claims.text: A machine-learning potential can be used to generate reference configurations for thermodynamic integration.
Machine-learning reference configurations can better represent the many atomic configurations of an ab initio liquid.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their high melting temperatures.
A deep-neural-network potential can describe solid and liquid structures and predict melting behavior in a high-entropy carbonitride.
Configurational entropy is relevant to phase stability in multicomponent alloys.
Configurational entropy can become increasingly important as the number of mixing species increases in disordered high-entropy carbides.
Improved representation of atomic configurations produces better reference–target phase-space overlap.
Better reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The machine-learning references will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed method will improve melting-temperature predictions.
The proposed method will improve phase-stability predictions.
TOR-TILD's EAM references are the baseline against which the proposed method should be evaluated.
The method is applicable to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in composition ranges where configurational entropy is significant.
The accuracy of machine-learning potentials is limited by training-data quality.
The accuracy of machine-learning potentials is limited by alloy-system complexity.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing machine-learning potentials with EAM references using melting temperature, phase stability, and configurational entropy as measurements.
Failure to show significant improvement over EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
